title: Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the strength of the Supreme Court:
1. The original Constitution provided for a Chief Justice and seven other judges.
2. Parliament can increase the number of judges by law.
3. Article 124 fixes the strength permanently at 34.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 124(1) leaves the number of judges to Parliament, which has raised it several times, most recently to 34 including the Chief Justice in 2019. The number is therefore not fixed by the Constitution.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Which of the following are qualifications for appointment as a Supreme Court judge under Article 124(3)?
1. A judge of a High Court for at least five years
2. An advocate of a High Court for at least ten years
3. A distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President
4. A district judge with ten years' experience
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: A candidate must be a citizen and meet one of the three routes: five years as High Court judge, ten years as High Court advocate, or distinguished jurist. District judges are not eligible directly, unless they qualify through the High Court bench.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Match List-I (Case) with List-II (Holding) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. First Judges Case (S.P. Gupta, 1981)
B. Second Judges Case (1993)
C. Third Judges Case (1998)
D. Fourth Judges Case (2015)
List-II
1. The Collegium for the Supreme Court comprises the CJI and four senior-most judges
2. The opinion of the CJI has primacy and the Collegium system was evolved
3. Executive had primacy in judicial appointments; 'consultation' did not mean concurrence
4. The NJAC Act and 99th Amendment were struck down
questions.e: In 1981 the Court held that 'consultation' did not mean concurrence, but in 1993 it reversed this and gave primacy to the CJI; the 1998 Presidential Reference fixed the five-member Collegium. In 2015 the NJAC was struck down, restoring the Collegium.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Judicial appointments; Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Assn v UoI
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC):
1. The Supreme Court struck it down unanimously.
2. It was introduced by the 99th Constitutional Amendment through Article 124A.
3. The Court held that it violated the independence of the judiciary, a basic feature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The decision of October 2015 was by a 4:1 majority, with Justice Chelameswar dissenting. The majority held that executive participation in the selection of judges compromises judicial independence.
questions.s: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Assn v UoI (2015); Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Under the Collegium system as evolved by the Third Judges Case (1998), the Collegium for recommending the appointment of Supreme Court judges consists of
o: the Chief Justice of India and the two senior-most judges
the Chief Justice of India and the four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court
the Chief Justice of India and the Law Minister
the Chief Justice of India and the Attorney General
questions.e: For the High Courts, the Collegium consists of the CJI and two senior-most judges. The recommendation is then sent to the Union government for the President's formal appointment.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Judicial appointments; Third Judges Case (1998)
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Statement-I: By convention, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is appointed Chief Justice of India.
Statement-II: In the Second Judges Case (1993), the Supreme Court held that seniority must be followed in appointing the CJI.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: The Constitution does not mention seniority, but the Court held in 1993 that the senior-most judge found fit must be appointed, giving the convention judicial backing. Seniority protects the CJI's post from political selection.
questions.s: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Assn v UoI (1993); Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of a Supreme Court judge:
1. A motion needs to be adopted by each House by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of the members present and voting.
2. The grounds are proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
3. The Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 regulates the procedure.
4. The motion can be initiated only in the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 124(4) provides the special majority, and the motion is signed by 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members and may start in either House. The address is presented to the President in the same session.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the retired judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts:
1. A retired Supreme Court judge cannot plead or act in any court or before any authority in India.
2. A retired High Court judge cannot plead in the Supreme Court.
3. A retired High Court judge cannot plead in the High Court in which he served.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 124(7) puts the bar on Supreme Court judges, and Article 220 bars High Court judges only from the High Court in which they sat. The restriction is meant to prevent post-retirement favours.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 131:
1. It is exclusive.
2. It covers disputes between the Centre and one or more States, and between States.
3. A private citizen can be a party to the dispute if his rights are affected.
4. Disputes arising from pre-Constitution treaties are excluded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Article covers federal disputes involving a legal right, and no private party may be involved. Pre-Constitution treaties and similar documents are excluded.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 32 and 226:
1. Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, whereas Article 226 is not.
2. A High Court can issue writs for enforcing Fundamental Rights and for 'any other purpose'.
3. The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 can never be suspended.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 32 is the right to constitutional remedies, which Dr Ambedkar called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution. It can be suspended during an Emergency by a Presidential order under Article 359, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Writs; Arts 32, 226, 359
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Match List-I (Writ) with List-II (Meaning/Use) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Habeas Corpus
B. Mandamus
C. Prohibition
D. Quo Warranto
List-II
1. 'By what authority' - tests the legality of a claim to a public office
2. 'We command' - directs a public official to perform a duty
3. Forbids a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction
4. 'To have the body' - for producing a detained person before the court
questions.e: Habeas corpus protects personal liberty, mandamus enforces public duties, prohibition is issued by a higher court to stop a lower court exceeding jurisdiction, and quo warranto tests the right to a public office.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Writs; Arts 32, 226
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about writs:
1. Quo warranto can be issued in respect of any private office.
2. Habeas corpus can be issued against private individuals in cases of illegal detention.
3. Mandamus cannot be issued against the President or a Governor for the exercise of official functions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Quo warranto lies only for a substantive public office created by the Constitution or by statute, not a private or ministerial post. Habeas corpus applies to private detention as well, and Article 361 protects the President and Governors from such writs.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Writs; Art 361
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about judicial review in India:
1. Article 13 provides that laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void.
2. Judicial review applies only to executive actions and not to legislation.
3. In I.R. Coelho (2007), the Supreme Court held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 are open to review on the basis of the basic structure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Judicial review covers legislative as well as administrative action. In I.R. Coelho, the Court held that the Ninth Schedule cannot be used to put laws beyond review if they damage the basic structure, with 24 April 1973 (Kesavananda) as the cut-off.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Judicial Review; I.R. Coelho (2007)
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: In which case did a 13-judge Bench of the Supreme Court, by a 7:6 majority, hold that Parliament can amend the Constitution but cannot alter its basic structure?
o: Minerva Mills v Union of India (1980)
Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala (1973)
Maneka Gandhi v Union of India (1978)
questions.e: In Golaknath, the Court had earlier held that Parliament could not amend the Fundamental Rights at all; Kesavananda changed this by giving Parliament wide amending powers within the limit of the basic structure. Minerva Mills (1980) later applied it to strike down parts of the 42nd Amendment.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter; Kesavananda Bharati (1973)
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Arrange the following landmark cases in chronological order:
1. Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
2. Golaknath v State of Punjab
3. Minerva Mills v Union of India
4. Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Golaknath (1967), Kesavananda Bharati (1973), Maneka Gandhi (1978) and Minerva Mills (1980). Together they trace the expansion of judicial protection against amendments and arbitrary state action.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter; Laxmikanth, Basic Structure
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Statement-I: In Maneka Gandhi v Union of India (1978), the Supreme Court held that the procedure established by law under Article 21 must be just, fair and reasonable.
Statement-II: The judgment read Articles 14, 19 and 21 together as protecting against arbitrary action.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Before this, A.K. Gopalan (1950) read Article 21 narrowly as only requiring a procedure prescribed by law. Linking Articles 14, 19 and 21 allowed the Court to test procedures for reasonableness, expanding Article 21 enormously.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Fundamental Rights; Maneka Gandhi (1978)
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the right to privacy case, K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India (2017):
1. A nine-judge Bench held privacy to be a Fundamental Right.
2. The Court overruled M.P. Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962) to the extent they held that there is no right to privacy.
3. The judgment was delivered by a five-judge Bench.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court held privacy to be intrinsic to life and liberty under Article 21 and to other freedoms in Part III. A nine-judge bench was needed because earlier eight- and six-judge decisions had denied the right.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Fundamental Rights; Puttaswamy (2017)
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Public Interest Litigation (PIL):
1. Only a person whose own rights are directly violated can file a PIL.
2. Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer were among the pioneers of PIL in India.
3. Hussainara Khatoon v State of Bihar (1979), on undertrial prisoners, is regarded as the first PIL case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PIL relaxes the traditional rule of locus standi, so any public-spirited person can approach the court on behalf of those who cannot, even by a letter (epistolary jurisdiction). This is why statement 1 is wrong.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: The Vishaka guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in 1997 relate to
o: the prevention of sexual harassment of women at the workplace
compensation to victims of industrial disasters
questions.e: In the absence of legislation, the Court laid down binding guidelines in a PIL, which were later replaced by the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013. This is a classic example of the Court filling a legislative vacuum.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / PIL; Vishaka v State of Rajasthan (1997)
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: The principle of 'absolute liability' for industries engaged in hazardous activities was evolved by the Supreme Court in
o: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v Union of India (1996)
Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v Union of India (1996)
M.C. Mehta v Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak case, 1986)
Bandhua Mukti Morcha v Union of India (1984)
questions.e: The Court rejected the English rule in Rylands v Fletcher, which has exceptions, and held that an enterprise engaged in a hazardous activity is absolutely liable with no exceptions. Vellore Citizens is associated with the precautionary principle.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Statement-I: Judicial activism has led to the expansion of the scope of Article 21.
Statement-II: Judicial overreach occurs when courts encroach on the domain of the legislature and the executive, undermining the separation of powers.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but Statement-II describes a distinct concern, not the reason for the expansion of Article 21. Activism protects rights where the other organs fail; overreach is when this crosses the line into policy making.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter / Judicial Activism
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of High Court judges:
1. They are appointed by the President after consulting the CJI, the Governor of the State and the Chief Justice of the High Court.
2. A distinguished jurist can be appointed as a High Court judge.
3. A candidate must have held a judicial office for ten years or been a High Court advocate for ten years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 217 sets these conditions. The 'distinguished jurist' route exists only for the Supreme Court (Article 124(3)).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter; High Court chapter; Art 217
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: The question of the age of a High Court judge, if it arises, is decided by
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, and his decision is final
A Bench of three Supreme Court judges
questions.e: Under Article 217(3), High Court judges retire at 62 and the President decides any age dispute after consulting the CJI. The Supreme Court retirement age is 65.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the High Court are correct?
1. The President can transfer a judge from one High Court to another after consulting the CJI.
2. Additional judges can be appointed for a period not exceeding two years.
3. A retired judge can be requested to sit and act as a judge of the High Court.
4. The President can appoint an acting Chief Justice when the office is vacant.
questions.e: All four are correct under Articles 222, 224, 224A and 223. These provisions help clear backlog and avoid vacancies, though they are used with caution to protect judicial independence.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles gives a High Court the power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals within its territorial jurisdiction (except those dealing with the armed forces)?
questions.e: Article 227 gives general supervisory powers, such as calling for returns and framing rules. Article 235 gives control over the district courts and subordinate judiciary (posting, promotion), and Article 228 allows a High Court to withdraw cases involving constitutional questions.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about subordinate courts:
1. District judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court.
2. An advocate of seven years' standing is eligible to be appointed as a district judge.
3. The control over district courts is vested in the Supreme Court.
4. Judicial officers other than district judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the State Public Service Commission and the High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Articles 233, 234 and 235 give the High Court a major role in the working of the subordinate judiciary. Control over district courts, including posting and promotion, lies with the High Court, not the Supreme Court.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lok Adalats:
1. They have statutory status under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
2. The award of a Lok Adalat is deemed to be a decree of a civil court and no appeal lies against it.
3. A Lok Adalat can try non-compoundable criminal offences.
4. The court fee paid is refunded if the case is settled at the Lok Adalat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The system gives quick and inexpensive justice, but a Lok Adalat can deal only with compoundable offences and cases both parties agree to settle. If parties are not satisfied, they can go to court.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Lok Adalat; Legal Services Authorities Act 1987
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about legal aid:
1. Article 39A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment, directs the State to provide free legal aid.
2. The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) was constituted under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
3. The Executive Chairman of NALSA is the Chief Justice of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CJI is the Patron-in-Chief, while the Executive Chairman is a serving or retired judge of the Supreme Court nominated by the President in consultation with the CJI. NALSA started functioning in 1995.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Permanent Lok Adalats:
1. They have jurisdiction over non-compoundable offences.
2. They deal with disputes relating to public utility services.
3. They can decide a dispute on its merits if the parties fail to reach a settlement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: They were introduced by a 2002 amendment to the Legal Services Authorities Act, and unlike regular Lok Adalats, they can adjudicate if conciliation fails. They have no jurisdiction over non-compoundable offences.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Lok Adalat; Legal Services Authorities (Amendment) Act 2002
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about Gram Nyayalayas are correct?
1. They were established under the Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008.
2. They may hold mobile courts.
3. The presiding officer, called Nyayadhikari, is appointed by the State Government in consultation with the High Court.
4. Appeals from their decisions lie directly to the Supreme Court.
questions.e: These village-level courts aim to bring justice to the doorsteps of rural citizens, but appeals lie to the district or sessions court and not directly to the Supreme Court.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Subordinate Courts chapter; Gram Nyayalayas Act 2008
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Statement-I: The decisions of Tribunals set up under Articles 323A and 323B are subject to the writ jurisdiction of the High Courts.
Statement-II: In L. Chandra Kumar v Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court held that judicial review is part of the basic structure and that the exclusion of High Courts' jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227 is unconstitutional.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Articles 323A and 323B were added by the 42nd Amendment, and the Court in 1997 held that tribunals work as substitutes for High Courts only at the first instance. Their decisions are therefore subject to scrutiny by a Division Bench of the concerned High Court.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal (NGT):
1. It was established under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.
2. It replaced the National Environment Appellate Authority.
3. Appeals against its orders lie to the Supreme Court.
4. It is strictly bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The NGT is guided by the principles of natural justice and is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure. It deals with civil cases relating to environmental laws specified in the Act.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to pass any order necessary to do 'complete justice' in any matter pending before it?
questions.e: Article 141 makes the Supreme Court's law binding on all courts, Article 143 concerns advisory jurisdiction, and Article 144 requires civil and judicial authorities to act in aid of the Court. Article 142 is the Court's unique power to fill gaps in the law.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts within the territory of India.
2. The advisory opinion given under Article 143 is binding on the President.
3. The Supreme Court has the power to review its own judgments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 141 binds all courts and Article 137 allows review. The Court's advisory opinion under Article 143 is not binding on the President, and the Court may even decline to answer a reference, as it did in the Ayodhya reference of 1993.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 136:
1. The Supreme Court may grant special leave to appeal against any judgment of any court or tribunal in the territory of India.
2. The power does not extend to the orders of tribunals relating to the armed forces.
3. The power can be exercised only against the judgments of High Courts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 136 is a discretionary and residuary power that can be exercised in respect of any court or tribunal, and Article 136(2) excludes armed forces tribunals. It is not limited to the High Courts.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Under Article 145(3), a minimum number of Supreme Court judges must sit to decide a case involving a substantial question of law on the interpretation of the Constitution. That number is
questions.e: Such Benches are called Constitution Benches. Larger benches of seven, nine or eleven judges are constituted to decide matters that require reconsideration of earlier decisions.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ad hoc judges of the Supreme Court can be appointed only from retired Supreme Court judges.
2. The Supreme Court sits in Delhi, but the CJI can, with the President's approval, appoint other places for its sittings.
3. A retired Supreme Court judge may be requested by the CJI, with the President's consent, to sit and act as a judge of the Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 127, an ad hoc judge is a High Court judge qualified for appointment to the Supreme Court, not a retired Supreme Court judge. Retired judges can be asked to sit under Article 128.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of judges:
1. Justice V. Ramaswami was the first judge against whom a motion for removal was moved in Parliament.
2. The motion was adopted by the Lok Sabha but failed in the Rajya Sabha.
3. The Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 provides for an inquiry committee before the motion is voted on.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1993 motion failed in the Lok Sabha itself, as it could not secure the required special majority, with many members abstaining. The Act requires a three-member committee to investigate charges once a motion is admitted.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter; Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Which of the following has NOT been held by the Supreme Court to be a part of the basic structure of the Constitution?
questions.e: Right to property was removed from the Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment and is now a constitutional right under Article 300A, not part of the basic structure. Judicial review, federalism and secularism have been repeatedly affirmed as basic features.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Basic Structure; Kesavananda, S.R. Bommai
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Match List-I (Doctrine) with List-II (Meaning) and select the correct answer using the code given below.
List-I
A. Doctrine of Severability
B. Doctrine of Eclipse
C. Doctrine of Pith and Substance
D. Colourable Legislation
List-II
1. A legislature cannot do indirectly what it cannot do directly
2. Only the unconstitutional part of a law is void if it can be separated
3. A pre-Constitution law inconsistent with a Fundamental Right becomes dormant, not dead
4. The true nature of a law is examined to decide which List it falls under
questions.e: Severability saves the valid part of a law; the doctrine of eclipse shows that an inconsistent law is only overshadowed by the Fundamental Right and revives if the obstacle is removed; pith and substance settles conflicts of legislative competence; colourable legislation bars indirect transgression.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: The Federal Court of India, the predecessor of the Supreme Court, was established under the
questions.e: The Federal Court began functioning in 1937 in Delhi. The Supreme Court was inaugurated on 28 January 1950 and replaced it, also taking over the role of the Privy Council as the final appellate court.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter; Evolution of the Judiciary
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about High Courts in India:
1. Article 231 allows Parliament to establish a common High Court for two or more States.
2. The Bombay High Court has jurisdiction over Goa and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.
3. The Kerala High Court has jurisdiction over Puducherry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Puducherry comes under the Madras High Court, while the Kerala High Court's jurisdiction covers Lakshadweep. Common High Courts exist because small States may not need their own bench.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the Supreme Court's jurisdiction are correct?
1. The Supreme Court is a court of record under Article 129.
2. It has the power to punish for its contempt.
3. Its advisory jurisdiction is exercised on a reference by the President.
4. Its original jurisdiction under Article 32 is exclusive and cannot be exercised by High Courts.
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Article 32 jurisdiction is not exclusive since High Courts can also issue writs under Article 226 to enforce Fundamental Rights; only Article 131 original jurisdiction is exclusive.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the contempt powers of the courts:
1. Truth is not available as a defence in any circumstances.
2. The Supreme Court and High Courts are courts of record.
3. The Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 distinguishes between civil and criminal contempt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Articles 129 and 215 make the superior courts courts of record. A 2006 amendment to the Act allowed truth as a defence if it is in public interest and the request is bona fide.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter; Contempt of Courts Act 1971
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Which Article of the Directive Principles of State Policy directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in public services?
questions.e: Article 50 supports judicial independence by separating judicial and executive functions. Article 39A relates to free legal aid, Article 46 to the weaker sections and Article 51 to international peace.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Supreme Court, in the Second Judges Case (1993), held that the 'consultation' with the Chief Justice of India in appointing judges means 'concurrence'.
Statement-II: Judicial independence, which is a basic feature, requires that the executive should not have a dominant role in the appointment of judges.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Court reasoned that the judiciary is best placed to judge a candidate's merit, and that executive primacy would endanger independence. This replaced the position in the S.P. Gupta case (1981).
questions.s: Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Assn v UoI (1993); Laxmikanth, Supreme Court chapter
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's criminal and civil appellate jurisdiction:
1. An appeal lies to the Supreme Court if a High Court on appeal reverses an acquittal and sentences the accused to death.
2. An appeal lies in every criminal case without any certificate.
3. An appeal lies if the High Court has withdrawn a case for trial to itself and sentenced the accused to death.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 134(1)(a) and (b) give these two appeals as of right. Other criminal appeals need a High Court certificate under Article 134(1)(c) or special leave under Article 136, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution provides for the High Court's power to issue writs, wider than the Supreme Court's power under Article 32?
questions.e: Article 226 lets High Courts issue writs for enforcing Fundamental Rights and also for any other purpose, so it also covers ordinary legal rights. Article 32 is limited to Fundamental Rights.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court and the independence of the judiciary:
1. The salaries and allowances of Supreme Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. The conduct of a judge cannot be discussed in Parliament except on a motion for his removal.
3. Salaries of judges can be reduced at any time by Parliament by an ordinary law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Charging salaries on the Consolidated Fund puts them beyond annual voting, and Article 121 bars discussion of a judge's conduct. Their emoluments cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment except during a Financial Emergency.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the power to transfer and withdraw cases:
1. Under Article 139A, the Supreme Court can transfer cases only from one High Court to another High Court.
2. Under Article 139A, the Supreme Court can withdraw cases pending before High Courts involving the same substantial question of law of general importance and decide them itself.
3. Under Article 228, a High Court can withdraw a case from a subordinate court if it involves a substantial question of law about the interpretation of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 139A also lets the Supreme Court transfer cases from a court in one State to a court in another, so the word 'only' makes statement 1 wrong. These powers help to ensure uniform interpretation and avoid conflicting decisions.
